questions.q: Why can't Castlebridge just copy its parent flow directly into the test environment without using a solution?
options: Flows cannot be copied between environments under any circumstances
The flow depends on other components, like the custom connector and the child flow, that won't exist in the new environment unless they move with it
Copied flows always run slower than imported ones
Test environments only accept flows, never connectors
questions.explain: A flow is rarely self-contained. Castlebridge's parent flow depends on a custom connector and a child flow being present. A solution bundles all of those dependencies together so the whole package can be imported and still work.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an unmanaged and a managed solution?
options: Unmanaged solutions are smaller in file size
An unmanaged solution is fully editable, used in development; a managed solution is locked down, used in test and production
Managed solutions cannot contain flows
There is no functional difference — it is only a naming convention
questions.explain: Unmanaged solutions are meant for active development and stay fully editable. Managed solutions are locked down after import, protecting test and production from accidental edits.

questions.q: What does Solution Checker do, and when should Castlebridge run it?
options: It automatically fixes any errors found in a solution
It inspects a solution for problems, ideally run before every export so issues are caught while still cheap to fix
It checks whether a solution's name is unique in the tenant
It is only available after a solution has already been imported into production
questions.explain: Solution Checker reviews a solution for issues. Running it before export catches problems while they're still inexpensive to fix, rather than after they've reached test or production.

questions.q: What is the normal ALM path a Power Platform customization follows, from Castlebridge's dev environment onward?
options: Production first, then test, then dev
Unmanaged in dev, exported, imported as managed into test, validated, then imported as managed into production
Dev and production share the same solution file with no export step
Managed in dev, unmanaged everywhere after
questions.explain: The standard path is: build unmanaged in dev, export, import as managed into test to validate, then move that same managed package into production.

questions.q: Why do the custom connector, the child flow, and the parent flow all belong inside the same solution?
options: Because Power Automate limits each environment to one solution total
Because whatever is listed as part of a solution travels together when that solution is exported, keeping dependent components together
Because only flows inside a solution can be edited
Because solutions can only ever contain exactly three components
questions.explain: A solution's object list determines what moves together on export. Keeping dependent components — the connector and both flows — in the same solution ensures none of them is missing when the package is imported elsewhere.
